o: From a user-activity log we need users who have BOTH free_trial and paid activity, reporting their average daily duration during trial days and during paid days, rounded to two decimals. Users 2 (never paid) are excluded; user 4 counts despite later cancelling. Conditional aggregation inside GROUP BY handles this cleanly: filter to users having a paid row, then average with CASE per activity type.
k: A HAVING clause (or IN subquery) keeps only converters.
AVG ignores NULLs, so CASE WHEN per type computes each average independently.
ROUND to 2 decimals; order by user_id.

a.i: Group all rows by user_id, keep groups containing a paid row, and average durations per activity_type via CASE expressions.
s: Compute both rounded averages and order by user_id.

c.python:
-- Same SQL for all languages (this is a Database problem).
SELECT user_id,
       ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN activity_type = 'free_trial' THEN activity_duration END), 2) AS trial_avg_duration,
       ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN activity_type = 'paid' THEN activity_duration END), 2) AS paid_avg_duration
FROM UserActivity
GROUP BY user_id
HAVING SUM(activity_type = 'paid') > 0
ORDER BY user_id;
